name: Margaret I Unites Scandinavia
summary: After her son Olaf IV died in 1387, Margaret became regent of Denmark and Norway, then secured the Swedish throne after deposing Albert of Mecklenburg in 1389. She was the driving force behind the Kalmar Union (1397), which united all three Scandinavian kingdoms under a single monarch. Governing until her death in 1412, she restored royal authority over fractious Nordic nobility through shrewd diplomacy and selective coercion.
outcomes: Margaret regent of all three kingdoms
Most effective ruler in Scandinavian medieval history

_quarry.structural_significance: The most capable ruler of medieval Scandinavia; created a Nordic union that shaped the political landscape until 1523.
